claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you're asking about your son Alex who is 8 years old.

To determine your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask you a few more questions:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your relationship and responsibility for Alex:

**Do you live with Alex, or if not, do you contribute at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards his upkeep (such as for food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me. But I do help out - I give about £10 a week towards his upkeep, you know, to help with things he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess whether your contributions are sufficient, I need to know a bit more:

**For how long has Alex been living away from you - is this a recent change or has it been more than 8 weeks?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been a few months now - he's been in local authority care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that Alex has been in local authority care for a few months.

This is important information. I need to ask:

**Does Alex spend any regular time at home with you? For example, does he spend at least 24 hours a week at home, or does he stay overnight with you for 2 nights in a row each week, or for 7 days or more in a row?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't come home to stay with me. He's at the care home full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I need to clarify one more thing about your situation:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure if anyone else is claiming it for him at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you would **not be eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

Alex has been in local authority care for several months, which is more than the 8-week limit. According to the Child Benefit rules, when a child is in care for more than 8 weeks, you can only continue to receive Child Benefit if the child spends at least 24 hours a week at home with you.

Since Alex is in care full-time and doesn't spend any regular time at home with you, this exception doesn't apply. While it's positive that you contribute £10 per week towards his upkeep, this contribution alone isn't sufficient to maintain eligibility when a child is in care for an extended period.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future - for example, if he starts spending at least 2 consecutive nights per week at home or 7 days or more in a row with you - you may be able to claim Child Benefit again. In that case, you should contact HMRC to discuss your situation.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about this decision?

reasonings: Alex is 8 years old and has been in local authority care for several months. According to the rules, Child Benefit payments are affected if a child goes into care for more than 8 weeks. The claimant does not live with Alex, and Alex does not spend regular time at home (no 24 hours per week, no 2 consecutive nights per week, and no 7+ days in a row at home). While the claimant contributes £10 per week towards Alex's upkeep, this amount is less than the standard Child Benefit payment (which is currently £25.60 per week for the eldest/only child or £16.95 for additional children). The rules state that to continue receiving Child Benefit after 8 weeks in care, the child must spend at least 24 hours a week at home, which does not apply here. Therefore, the claimant would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex under these circumstances.
